data.text:
F25 is fixed at records 113 and 114, and verified independently of the implementer that
wrote it. It was recorded in note 106 as an unreproduced failure and an unbounded table.
Both halves are now settled, and the first one turned out to have a cause worth the chase.

## The failure was a deadlock, and the mechanism reproduces on demand

Twelve runs of the suite were green after note 106, on top of five earlier, and the
failure looked like a ghost. It appeared again the first time the suite was run with
coverage enabled, and this time it carried its own diagnosis: `erasingTheTenant` answered
`40P01`, which is `deadlock_detected`, where `accepted` was expected.

`vitest.config.ts` set no pool option, so vitest's default applied and test files ran in
parallel workers against one local database. This package's files carry about twenty
schema-mutating statements between them. A `drop constraint` takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
lock on `public.claims` while another file is seeding all 29 tables.

Reproduced directly rather than inferred, in two concurrent sessions of that shape:

| session | statement | answer |
|---|---|---|
| seeding | `insert into public.claims` | refused **40P01** |
| schema-changing | lock on `public.tenants` | accepted |

Same SQLSTATE the reported failure carried. The probe left nothing behind.

That also explains the original run in note 106, which predates the test that failed here:
it was the same class of collision from F19's or F23's schema-mutating tests. A race needs
its timing, which is why seventeen runs could pass in a row and prove nothing.

## What the evidence for the fix is, and is not

The implementer ran the suite 40 times with coverage after the fix, all green, and said
plainly in record 115 that this is weak evidence on its own, because 20 consecutive runs
with coverage were green before the fix too. That is the right way to report a race, and
it is why the mechanism demonstration above is what the fix rests on rather than a count
of green runs. Six further coverage runs here were green.

The tombstone half has evidence of the ordinary kind, because it is not a race.
`seen.erased_tenants` grew about 13 rows per run before and stands unmoved at 481 across
46 runs since. Measured here: 481 before six coverage runs and 481 after.

It is worth repeating what that half is not. Every tenant id in the suite is
server-generated and never supplied, so no test could ever have collided with a tombstone
and the growth could not have caused a failure. It was fixed because an unbounded table in
every developer's database is worth not having.

## The coverage decision, and F26

The `include` was deliberately not widened, and the reasoning is measured rather than
asserted: `db/**/*.ts` reports 89.69 per cent against the baseline of 100.0 recorded in
`docs/harness/coverage.json`, so widening puts the floor under the baseline and the only
way through is to move the baseline, which is a delivery decision and the harness's file.
The second reason is the better one: what the wider figure would measure is a constants
module and a routing-table parser, while this ticket's work is five SQL migrations that no
line-coverage provider instruments. Swapping a number that says nothing about the schema
for another number that says nothing about the schema is not an improvement.

**F26 is new and corrects this journal.** Note 70 said the coverage figure measures none of
`packages/core/db/` and blamed the `--` that pnpm forwards in `harness/coverage.py:19`.
That was incomplete. `coverage.include` is `['src/**/*.ts']` and `db/` is not under `src/`,
so even with the `--` fixed the summary could never have measured `db/`. Both defects had
to hold at once for the figure to be as meaningless as it was, and a third question sits
behind them: what a line-coverage floor should mean for a package whose work is SQL. All
three belong to whoever owns the harness fix.

F19 to F25 are now fixed. F26 is open and is not this ticket's to close.
